taxonomy.subtopic: NADPH-dependent glutathione regeneration during oxidant stress

questions.stem_html: A 28-year-old man develops fatigue, jaundice, and dark urine two days after receiving rasburicase. Laboratory studies show an increased reticulocyte count, indirect hyperbilirubinemia, elevated lactate dehydrogenase, and decreased haptoglobin. A peripheral smear shows bite cells; supravital staining reveals erythrocyte inclusions. The accompanying pathway diagram highlights a deficient reaction in the pentose phosphate pathway. Which downstream process is most directly impaired?

options.text_html: Regeneration of reduced glutathione from oxidized glutathione
Conversion of methemoglobin iron from the ferric to the ferrous state by cytochrome b5 reductase
Production of ATP from phosphoenolpyruvate by pyruvate kinase
Conjugation of bilirubin with glucuronic acid in hepatocytes
Assembly of alpha- and beta-globin chains into hemoglobin tetramers

questions.explanation_html: G6PD catalyzes the first, rate-limiting step of the pentose phosphate pathway and supplies NADPH. Glutathione reductase uses NADPH to regenerate reduced glutathione, which allows glutathione peroxidase to detoxify hydrogen peroxide. During oxidant exposure, inadequate NADPH causes glutathione depletion, hemoglobin denaturation into Heinz bodies, membrane injury, and formation of bite cells when splenic macrophages remove the inclusions.

wrong_choice_explanations.2: Cytochrome b5 reductase deficiency causes congenital methemoglobinemia; it is not the principal mechanism of oxidant-triggered hemolysis in G6PD deficiency.
wrong_choice_explanations.3: Pyruvate kinase generates ATP in glycolysis. Its deficiency produces chronic hemolysis through ATP depletion rather than impaired antioxidant defense.
wrong_choice_explanations.4: Bilirubin conjugation occurs in hepatocytes and may affect jaundice severity, but it does not cause Heinz bodies or bite cells.
wrong_choice_explanations.5: Globin-chain assembly defects produce hemoglobinopathies or thalassemias rather than acute oxidant-induced hemolysis.

questions.educational_objective: G6PD-derived NADPH maintains reduced glutathione in erythrocytes; deficiency permits oxidant injury, Heinz body formation, and bite-cell hemolysis.

media.alt_text: Original pentose phosphate and glutathione pathway showing how G6PD-derived NADPH supports peroxide detoxification and prevents hemoglobin oxidation.
